info.name: Clinical Scenario: CareTeam Management
info.description:
# Clinical Relevance
Care teams are groups of primary care staff members who collectively take responsibility for a set of patients. Care teams blend multidisciplinary skills, focusing several people’s insights, rather than a single physician’s, on each patient’s problems (AHRQ). A care team may consist of nurses, physicians, medical assistants, schedulers, and more. Care teams need efficient and secure tools in order to collaborate effectively and deliver better patient care. 


# Objectives of this Collection
* Review how Commure’s FHIR® API can help you create applications to allow clinicians to view their patient lists, read, write, and share notes about individual patients.
* Review the basic concepts of FHIR. 

# Scenario Summary
This collection goes through the following user journey:
1. A doctor uses a front end FHIR client application to view their care teams (via the [CareTeam](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/CareTeam.html) resource).  
2. The doctor selects a specific care team.
3. The doctor selects a group of patients that belong to a specific care team (via the [Group](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/Group.html) resource).
4. The doctor selects a patient.
5. The doctor reads the patient’s information and other doctors’ notes on the patient (via the [ClinicalImpression](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/ClinicalImpression.html) resource).
6. The doctor adds a new note to the patient (via the [ClinicalImpression](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/ClinicalImpression.html) resource).

# FHIR Concepts covered
FHIR offers a very effective set of resources to manage patients and groups of patients. The scenario presented here is a simplified example to introduce FHIR’s resources. We will interact with the following resources:
[Patient](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/Patient.html), [Group](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/Group.html), [CareTeam](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/CareTeam.html), [Practitioner](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/Practitioner.html), [PractitionerRole](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/PractitionerRole.html), [ClinicalImpression](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/ClinicalImpression.html)

# Quickstart
To navigate a scenario using the Postman collection you will need to
1. Sign up [here](https://accounts.commure.com/signin/register) and accept Commure’s Terms and Conditions.
2. Authenticate (To have more information about it read the [postman documentation](https://learning.postman.com/docs/sending-requests/authorization/#oauth-20), our [documentation](https://developer.commure.com/docs/apis/auth/introduction) or see our [authentication collection](https://documenter.getpostman.com/view/4955094/TVYAffgd)).
3. Set up the initial FHIR data you need using the first request of the collection
4. Go through the user journey performing each request in the collection

# How to authenticate
Once you are signed up, there are two ways to authenticate with Commure’s Server:

## Alternative A:

Click the “View more actions” button of the Collection > Click “Edit” > Go to the variables tab and update only the tenant-id field (both initial value and current value) The tenant-id is the suffix on the baseurl when you sign in to the Commure’s Developer Platform. For example: in https://dashboard-99750511.developer.commure.com/smart/dashboard/ the tenant id is: 99750511. After updating this field please click “Update” at the bottom right corner of the window.  

Now click again the “View more actions” button of the Collection > Click “Edit” > and this time, go to the authorization tab > select Oauth2 as the authorization method > Click “Get New Access Token” > Fill the fields with your tenant information.  

> Remember to remove the blank space between the Curly braces `{ {tenant-id}}`


  * Callback url: http://localhost:1234/callback. 
  * Auth url:  `https://api-{ {tenant-id}}.developer.commure.com/auth/authorize`
  * Access Token url: `https://api-{ {tenant-id}}.developer.commure.com/auth/token`
  * client-id: smart_hello_world
  * Scope: openid email
  * Leave Client Secret and State empty.

  
After filling in the details, please Click in “Request Token” > In the next window Click “Use Token” >Once that window closes please click “Update”

## Alternative B:

In your browser go to the /auth endpoint, and get the authorization token, then use the token as a bearer in every request you want to make to our servers.

> Note: If you get a 404 SSL error, you forgot to set the tenant-id variable on the collections variables, or you have a wrong base url.

request.description:
For this scenario we will assume that the following data is already saved in the FHIR database:

* An Organization.
* A Patient.
* A Practitioner.
* A Practioner Role (This one is not needed but is a good practice to have reference to Practioner Roles and not to the Practioner because the person that is a practitioner could change or be replaced by another person, but the role does not change).
* A Group.
* A CareTeam.

This request will create all the data needed.

item.name: 2. Get the care teams for a specific practitioner

request.description: The client application can use the practitioner id to retrieve and display the practitioner information along with the care teams he has to care. A reference to the `Practitioner` resource is found in the `CareTeam` resource in the `participant` field. The same practitioner could be referenced in several care teams.

response.name: sucessfull get care team

header.value: CP="This is not a P3P policy."

request.description:
With the `CareTeam` resources retrieved, the client application can use the linked `Group` resource to retrieve and display the patients in the group. A reference to the `Patient` resource  is found in the `Group` resource in the field `member`, and a reference to the `Group` resource is found in the `CareTeam` resource in the field `subject`.

We are going to retrieve the `Group` resource.

header.value: CP="This is not a P3P policy."

item.name: 4. Get Patient info and notes about the patient

request.description:
The client application can use the patient id to retrieve and display the patient information along with the notes (`ClinicalImpression`) the practitioners have left about the patient. A reference to the `Patient` resource is found in the `ClinicalImpression` resource in the `subject` field. The same patient could be referenced in several  `ClinicalImpression` resources.

We are going to retrieve both the `Patient` and the `ClinicalImpression`.

response.name: sucesfull Get Patient info and notes about the patient

header.value: CP="This is not a P3P policy."

item.name: 5. Add a note to a Patient

request.description:
The client application can create notes about the patient (`ClinicalImpression`). A reference to the `Patient` resource is found in the `ClinicalImpression` resource in the `subject` field.
We are going to retrieve both the `Patient` and the `ClinicalImpression` resources.

response.name: sucessfull Add a note to a Patient
